record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.original_question: The generalized s-rule can be described using dot diagrams and, for irreducible brane junctions, in terms of self-intersection numbers of the holomorphic curves wrapped by M2-branes. Can one formulate a criterion for the generalized s-rule in terms of self-intersection numbers for reducible junctions?

evidence.quote: Question 7. Can we write down the criterion of generalized s-rule in terms of self-intersection numbers for reducible junctions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Consider Type IIB / M-theory configurations of (p,q) 5-brane webs (equivalently, the dual M-theory description in which BPS states arise from M2-branes wrapping holomorphic curves in a local Calabi–Yau threefold). To such a web one may attach additional brane junctions, and a fundamental consistency condition limiting how many such junctions can be simultaneously placed is known as the generalized s-rule. Two equivalent formulations are known in special cases:

(i) Dot-diagram criterion: For a web with attached 7-branes, the dot diagram records how the BPS string ends on the 7-branes, and the generalized s-rule can be stated combinatorially as a condition on allowed dot diagrams.

(ii) Self-intersection criterion (irreducible case): For an irreducible brane junction, i.e. one realized in M-theory by a single irreducible holomorphic curve C wrapped by an M2-brane in the local Calabi–Yau, the generalized s-rule is equivalent to the condition that the self-intersection number C·C (computed in the relevant surface, with appropriate boundary contributions) satisfies a definite inequality (so that C represents a genuine BPS state and the junction is supersymmetric).

A reducible junction is one whose corresponding holomorphic class decomposes as a sum C = C_1 + C_2 + … + C_k of two or more irreducible holomorphic curves, possibly with multiplicities, each wrapped by an M2-brane.

Problem. Formulate a precise criterion, expressed purely in terms of the self-intersection numbers C_i · C_i and the mutual intersection numbers C_i · C_j of the irreducible components, that is equivalent to the generalized s-rule for an arbitrary reducible brane junction C = ∑ n_i C_i. In particular, find a set of (in)equalities involving the matrix of intersection numbers (C_i · C_j) and the multiplicities n_i which holds if and only if the reducible junction is consistent with the generalized s-rule.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this question was located. The question is posed as an open problem in a list of open questions in quiver gauge theory, and web searches for a self-intersection-number criterion for the generalized s-rule on reducible brane junctions did not return any paper announcing a solution.

status_evidence.title: Self-Intersection Number of BPS Junctions in Backgrounds of Three and Seven-Branes
status_evidence.snippet: Self-intersection numbers of junctions have been used to constrain the BPS spectrum of N=2, D=4 theories arising on a D3-brane probe in a 7-brane background.
status_evidence.claim: The self-intersection-number characterization is established in the irreducible/BPS-junction setting, consistent with the problem's premise.
